To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a marginalized attentional network (MAN) to suppress the most salient responses of the most saliant regions and learn a set of latent probabilities to generate better class activations for temporal action localization.

we proposed a marginalized average aggregation (MAG) module that samples multiple subsets from video snippet features according the a set of latent probabilities, and we proved that the MAA can reduce the response difference between the most saliency regions and the others, which is beneficial for the weakly-supervised action localization task.

we propose a novel marginalized average attentional networks to alleviate the issue of overestimation of most salient regions by taking the expectation over the averaged subset features and reduce the complexity of the MAA from $2^T$ to $T^2$ in the temporal action localization task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel attentional network for weakly-supervised video understanding.
weakly supervised learning of action recognition and temporal action localization in videos.
the following questions: How to alleviate the overestimation issue of the most salienet regions in the weakly-supervised learning framework for temporal action localization?
